metadata.icdo_version: ICD-O-3.2. morphology_entries[] is GENERATED by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group IV from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed from an option file or a diagnostic pathway document (Group 4 build contract §1, §1.1). 8683 Gangliocytic paraganglioma exists in ICD-O-3.2 only at behaviour /0 and is absent from this file (build contract §0.2). 9504 Spongioneuroblastoma is retained and flagged obsolete_term though not marked [obs] by IARC -- no current WHO entity has been shown to live on its stem (build contract §2.3, ruling D2) -- and is unreachable from any tree. 9520, 9521 and 9523 are retained and reachable only by exact-string alias, at confidence_ceiling low, pending WHO Head and Neck Tumours 5th edition (ruling D3).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain terminator for the paraganglionic family: 8681, 8682, 8690, 8691, 8692, 8693 and 8700 all fall back here. WHO version recorded as "WHO 2022" (Mete O, et al. Overview of the 2022 WHO Classification of Paragangliomas and Pheochromocytomas. Endocrine Pathology 2022;33(1):90-114, PMID 35285002 -- full text read 16 Sep 2026 -- and the WHO Paediatric Tumours volume, both 2022) per build contract instruction (Group 4 build contract, pre-context table). NOTE the edition nuance recorded at contract §10.1: the fixed rule that all PPGLs (paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas) are behaviour-3 neoplasms with variable metastatic potential was already settled in the 4th edition, 2017, not the 5th: "Prior to the 2017 WHO classification (also known the 4th edition), PPGLs... were accompanied by the adjectives 'benign' or 'malignant'.... As a result, all PPGLs have been considered as malignant neoplasms with variable metastatic potential." (Mete 2022, p. 100). "WHO 2022" here names the edition that classifies and names the individual entities on this stem, not the edition that first fixed the behaviour. Mete 2022 never states an ICD-O code anywhere in the paper (contract §10.1) -- it corroborates that a current WHO entity lives on the stem; icdo32.sqlite states the number. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (pp. 96-106, full text read 16 Sep 2026): synaptophysin and chromogranin A are the general neuroendocrine markers the WHO panel recommends; GATA3 is the specific marker that separates a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma from a neuroblastic tumour at the same site (build contract §5.1); cytokeratin is negative in both families and separates neither from the other, only both from a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour. PHOX2B is not listed here: Mete 2022 discusses PHOX2B only under the neuroblastoma differential (p. 108), never as a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, and PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive (contract §5.1, §10.1). A branch citing PHOX2B for this family must cite Manethova 2023, not WHO. 8683 Gangliocytic paraganglioma is NOT built in this file (build contract §0.2): icdo32.sqlite carries it only at behaviour /0, and ICCC-3 Group IV declares behaviour 3 only, so there is no 8683/3 to author. Independently, Mete 2022 (p. 94) confirms WHO 2022 renamed the entity "composite gangliocytoma/neuroma and neuroendocrine tumor (CoGNET)", walking it out of the paraganglioma family entirely -- both legs of the two-source test agree it is removed. 8683 appears nowhere in this file as a morphology_code or alias target; it may only be an alias input resolving to a terminal that explains why it cannot be coded here and refers the case to the registrar. Whether WHO 2022 states an ICD-O code for CoGNET is unknown -- only the Mete 2022 abstract carries the CoGNET quote with no page number; the full text (p. 94) confirms it but still states no code.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, plus catecholamines and chromogranin A, together with an imaging-demonstrated adrenal (or, for the extra-adrenal presentation, paraspinal/retroperitoneal) mass at a site consistent with pheochromocytoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- catecholamines and chromogranin A -- as sufficient for coding 8700/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (here, the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Falls back to 8680, per ICCC-2017's placement of pheochromocytoma in subgroup IVb alongside the paragangliomas. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (pp. 96-106, full text read 16 Sep 2026): synaptophysin and chromogranin A are the general neuroendocrine markers the WHO panel recommends; GATA3 is the specific marker that separates a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma from a neuroblastic tumour at the same site (build contract §5.1); cytokeratin is negative in both families and separates neither from the other, only both from a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour. PHOX2B is not listed here: Mete 2022 discusses PHOX2B only under the neuroblastoma differential (p. 108), never as a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, and PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive (contract §5.1, §10.1). A branch citing PHOX2B for this family must cite Manethova 2023, not WHO. DIVERGENCE, recorded not acted on (build contract §4.2): Visser's own Table 4 (p. 06) places pheochromocytoma in Group XI, not Group IV. ICCC-2017 is Layer 1 and governs, and ICCC-2017 puts 8700 in IVb -- the routing does not change. One of the two Visser Table 4 rows this group owns (with 9500): catecholamines and chromogranin A plus imaging is a valid basis-4, no-tissue diagnosis for this code alone. confidence_ceiling set to medium, not high, because this entry documents that marker-plus-imaging pathway, which the ENCR basis system ranks below a histological or IHC-confirmed diagnosis; a tissue-confirmed pheochromocytoma is not itself lower confidence. COMPOSITE PPGL (composite paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma): icdo32.sqlite carries "Composite pheochromocytoma" as a Related term on this stem. Mete 2022 (p. 106) reports composite PPGL is about 75% pheochromocytoma-with-ganglioneuroma and about 10% each with neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma, described in adults ("fourth to fifth decade", p. 106). A composite case's ganglioneuroma component must not be routed to the D1 behaviour_exclusion terminal (build contract §3, §6 D1) -- the composite lesion as a whole stays coded to its pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma stem, not split into an excluded benign component plus a separate malignant one. Mete 2022's own abstract writes "composite paraganglioma" while the body always writes "composite PPGL" or "composite pheochromocytoma" -- an inconsistency in the source, recorded so nobody reconciles it silently (contract §10.1).

RULING D1 (build contract §2.1, §3, §6): 9490/0 is Ganglioneuroma, benign -- the fully matured end of the neuroblastic spectrum -- and is NOT authored in this file. ICCC-3 Group IV admits behaviour 3 only, so a ganglioneuroma is not a registrable Group IV cancer. This is the group's central trap: a tree that resolves "Schwannian stroma-dominant, maturing or mature" to the 9490 stem without checking behaviour would silently emit 9490/3 Ganglioneuroblastoma for a benign tumour. The behaviour_exclusion field (contract §3, ratified by the registrar) is how the tree (Tasks 4-6) must handle this -- a branch or terminal carrying it emits no morphology_code, states the lesion is 9490/0 Ganglioneuroma, benign, and refers the decision to the registrar. Precedent: Group 3 left 8000/6 and 8000/9 unauthored for the same reason. The REDCap option file lists "Ganglioneuroma" as if it were a 9490 option string -- it is not; it is 9490/0 and is not built here (build contract §0.3). CNS NOTE (build contract §0.6): icdo32.sqlite carries synonym or related terms tying this stem to the central nervous system -- yet ICCC-3 places this code in Group IVa at every site, including the CNS, and Group III does not claim it. This reads wrong to a reviewer who expects a CNS-sited tumour to route to Group III; it is not an error, it is how ICCC-3 states the group. Do not "fix" it by adding a CNS carve-out. (Related term here is "CNS ganglioneuroblastoma".) Falls back to 9500. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (p. 108) and the sympathoadrenal differential (build contract §5.1): PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; cytokeratin negative. PHOX2B does NOT separate this from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both families are PHOX2B positive; GATA3 and the sustentacular S100/SOX10 pattern are what separate them (contract §5.1, §10.1) -- do not add GATA3 to this entry's required panel, it is a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, not a neuroblastic one. Evidence: Shimada 1999 and Peuchmaur 2003 (the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee, INPC, classification), Monclair 2009 and Ambros 2005/2009 (the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group, INRG) -- the group's best-evidenced family, corroborated a second time by Mete 2022 Table 1 (p. 108), which independently reproduces the full INPC classification (undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, differentiating; intermixed, nodular; maturing, mature) attributed to Shimada 1999. who_version recorded WHO 2022 per the Mete 2022 / WHO Paediatric Tumours convergence; the underlying INPC criteria that actually separate this code from 9500 and from 9490/0 are Shimada 1999, predating either 2022 document.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated urinary homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA), together with an imaging-demonstrated mass at a site typical of a neuroblastic primary (adrenal, paraspinal/retroperitoneal, posterior mediastinal, or elsewhere along the sympathetic chain) consistent with neuroblastoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- urinary HVA and VMA -- as sufficient for coding 9500/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4, not basis 2. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain terminator for the neuroblastic family: 9490 falls back here. One of the two Visser Table 4 rows this group owns (with 8700): urinary HVA and VMA plus imaging is a valid basis-4, no-tissue diagnosis for this code alone -- the pathway's Stage-2C constellation is a Table 4 row, not a Table 3 row (build contract §4.2). confidence_ceiling set to medium, not high, because this entry documents that marker-plus-imaging pathway, which the ENCR basis system ranks below a histological or IHC-confirmed diagnosis (basis 7 or 9); a tissue- or bone-marrow-confirmed neuroblastoma is not itself lower confidence, it is simply not what this ceiling is bounding. CNS NOTE (build contract §0.6): icdo32.sqlite carries synonym or related terms tying this stem to the central nervous system -- yet ICCC-3 places this code in Group IVa at every site, including the CNS, and Group III does not claim it. This reads wrong to a reviewer who expects a CNS-sited tumour to route to Group III; it is not an error, it is how ICCC-3 states the group. Do not "fix" it by adding a CNS carve-out. (Synonyms here are "Central neuroblastoma" and "CNS neuroblastoma"; "Sympathicoblastoma" is also a synonym on this stem but is marked [obs].) IHC panel per Mete 2022 (p. 108) and the sympathoadrenal differential (build contract §5.1): PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin positive (NB84 and tyrosine hydroxylase are also named at p. 108 to separate neuroblastoma from rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour, Ewing sarcoma and lymphoblastic lymphoma, but are not carried here as they are not part of the closed field's minimal panel); cytokeratin negative. PHOX2B does NOT separate this from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive; GATA3 and the sustentacular S100/SOX10 pattern do (contract §5.1, §10.1). Evidence family: see 9490's note -- Shimada 1999, Peuchmaur 2003, Monclair 2009, Ambros 2005/2009, plus Okamatsu 2009, Ma 2021, Verly 2017 and Nakagawara 2018 (contract §10), the group's strongest-evidenced code.

DUAL-GROUP with Group III (build contract §1, §2.5, §6): ICCC-3 gives this code to Group III (subgroup IIIc3, behaviour 0-1,3) across the whole of C70.0-C72.9. No behaviour_exclusion terminal is built for it in this task since no tree references this stem yet; a future tree task must not silently emit 9501/3 for a benign lesion. Synonym "Diktyoma, malignant" is carried at behaviour /3 on this stem. No fallback: this is an unrelated entity to 9502, 9503 and 9504 despite the shared number range -- do not invent a chain among them to make the graph tidy (build contract, pre-context).

morphology_entries.coding_note: RULINGS D4 and D6 (build contract §2.4, §6). Verified against icdo32.sqlite 16 Sep 2026 and, at the registrar's instruction, cross-checked against both the 2019 draft workbook and the 9 Oct 2020 final source workbook so a conversion artefact or a draft-stage edit could be excluded: "Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor", "Peripheral neuroectodermal tumor" and "PPNET" are verbatim ICD-O-3.2 Synonym or Related terms on 9364/3 Ewing sarcoma, NOT on this stem. They alias to 9364 with a cross-group referral (Group VIII at bone, Group IX at soft tissue), never to 9503. 9364 must not appear as a morphology_code anywhere in this file (validation rule, build contract §8 item 8) -- verified: it does not. Alias-instruction entries 30, 31 and 33 (which sent these three strings to 9503) are wrong and are overridden; entry 29 ("Neuroepithelioma" alone) stands and stays on this stem. Unqualified "PNET, NOS" / "Primitive neuroectodermal tumor, NOS" are 9473/3, Group III -- also not aliased to this stem. D6: the exact phrase "peripheral neuroepithelioma" appears nowhere in ICD-O-3.2 -- not as a term, a synonym, a see-also, an inclusion or an exclusion. 9503/3 Neuroepithelioma, NOS is its only plausible home and its only ICD-O-3.2 term (icdo32.sqlite carries no synonym or related term on this stem at all); nothing in Layer 1 confirms the assignment. Ruled: alias "peripheral neuroepithelioma" to this stem, but route it through a branch that asks whether CD99 is positive with PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative (favouring the Ewing family / 9364 instead of resolving here) before resolving to this code at confidence_ceiling low, with an outstanding-workup row naming CD99, PHOX2B and synaptophysin when that panel is not done. ihc_markers_exclude carries CD99 for that reason -- CD99 positivity (with PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative) argues against this code and for 9364. DUAL-GROUP with Group III (build contract §1, §2.5, §6): ICCC-3 gives this code to Group III (subgroup IIIc3, behaviour 0-1,3) across the whole of C70.0-C72.9. Outside that range -- including C80.9, unknown/ill-defined primary -- it is Group IV (IVb). See this entry's topography_routing_note for the routing rule; presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules["9501-9504"] rule currently matches only C70.9, C71.9 and C72.9 and must be extended to the full C70.0-C72.9 range now that Group III is built -- that fix is out of scope for this file (contract §2.5, §7.2). Also see the topography_routing_note for the C70.0-C72.9 / Group III split, which applies to this code independently of the D4/D6 finding above -- a peripheral-site neuroepithelioma that also tests CD99-positive still refers to Group VIII/IX on histology grounds, not to Group III on topography grounds; the two rules do not interact. Out of scope, flagged not fixed here: presentation_router.json's 9260 dual-group rule still routes a code (9260/3) that ICD-O-3.2 no longer carries at behaviour /3 -- 9260 exists only at /0, Aneurysmal bone cyst. That is a Group VIII/IX defect; record it in docs/TODO.md, do not touch it here (contract §2.4).

morphology_entries.coding_note: RULING D2 (build contract §2.3, §6). obsolete_term is true; obsolete_source is NOT an [obs] marker -- icdo32.sqlite prints "Spongioneuroblastoma" on 9504/3 with no [obs] flag, so the Group 3 [obs] test does not remove it. It is retained and flagged obsolete_term instead because no current WHO entity has been shown to live on this stem: the term is a 1948 artefact with no modern diagnostic criteria, and Pfister 2022 (the group's assigned baseline, read in full 16 Sep 2026) does not discuss it or any peripheral medulloepithelioma/neuroepithelioma entity at all (contract §10). Precedent: Group 3's thirteen obsolete_term entries, which were flagged on the [obs] ground -- this entry is flagged on the no-current-WHO-entity ground instead, which is a different finding and must not be conflated with an IARC [obs] marking. Reachable from no tree (validation rule, build contract §8 item 4) -- exists only so a historical record or an exact-string alias input carrying this term resolves. who_version recorded ICD-O-3.2, not a WHO edition. No fallback: unrelated entity to 9501, 9502 and 9503 despite the shared number range.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: ICCC-3 gives this code to Group III (subgroup IIIc3, behaviour 0-1,3) across the whole of C70.0-C72.9 (brain, spinal cord and other parts of the central nervous system). Outside that range -- including C80.9, unknown/ill-defined primary site -- it is Group IV (IVb). Route by topography at Stage 1: C70.0-C72.9 goes to Group III; every other Group-IV-carriable site goes to Group IV. presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules["9501-9504"] rule must extend its topography_in to the full C70.0-C72.9 range now that Group III is built (build contract §2.5) -- that fix is out of scope for this file.
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: Not an IARC [obs] marking -- icdo32.sqlite carries "Spongioneuroblastoma" on 9504/3 as a plain Preferred term, unflagged. The obsolescence finding is this build's own, made on the Group 3 test ("a code leaves the decision tree only when no current WHO entity lives on its stem"): the term is an 1948-era artefact with no modern diagnostic criteria, and no current WHO volume, including Pfister SM, et al., Cancer Discovery 2022;12(2):331-355 (PMID 34921008), the group's assigned baseline, has been shown to discuss it. Do not attribute this to IARC or cite it as an [obs] term.

Chain terminator for the olfactory family: 9520, 9521 and 9523 all fall back here, and it is the only one of the four olfactory codes a histological differential branch may resolve to (ruling D3, build contract §6). Synonym "Esthesioneuroblastoma" is carried on this stem in icdo32.sqlite, with the code reference (C30.0) printed against the term itself in the source. Manethova 2023 supplies a negative PHOX2B finding for this entity -- unlike neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma (9490, 9500), which are PHOX2B positive (build contract §5.1, §10.1), this entity is reported PHOX2B negative, recorded here in ihc_markers_exclude: a PHOX2B-positive small round cell tumour in the sinonasal region argues against this code and for a sympathetic/metastatic neuroblastic process instead. Synaptophysin and chromogranin A are carried as the general neuroendocrine markers. Veyrat (Advances in Oto-Rhino-Laryngology vol. 84, 2020, pp. 154-167, abstract only) confirms Kadish and Hyams as the two staging/grading systems in clinical use but reproduces neither table and does not state an ICD-O code. The Hyams grade table circulating in the pathway document has no citable primary source -- it traces to Wenig BM, Hyams VJ, Heffner DK, a LARYNX paper (Cancer 1988;62(12):2658-76, PMID 3056608), wrong tumour and wrong organ, not to Hyams VJ's actual olfactory neuroblastoma chapter in the AFIP Fascicle 25 (1988), which PubMed does not index -- and must not be asserted as fact (contract §10.2 item 2); a tree may record the grade string a report states, without asserting what the grades mean. Kadish staging is settled and is three groups, A-C (Kadish, Goodman, Wang, Cancer 1976;37(3):1571-6, PMID 1260676, from the abstract); stage D is not Kadish's, it is Morita, et al., Neurosurgery 1993;32(5):706-14, PMID 8492845 (contract §10.2 item 3) -- correct the attribution wherever a tree or its documentation names it. Staging and grading are not coding inputs: 9522/3 is 9522/3 at every Kadish stage and every Hyams grade. who_version recorded as "ICD-O-3.2", not a WHO edition: no current WHO volume has been shown to cover this entity. Pfister SM, et al. A Summary of the Inaugural WHO Classification of Pediatric Tumors: Transitioning from the Optical into the Molecular Era. Cancer Discovery 2022;12(2):331-355, PMID 34921008, PMC9401511 -- the group's assigned baseline, read in full 16 Sep 2026 -- does not discuss it at all.
